applied.quote: When the repurchase is for an IRA or Roth IRA, Publication 550 excepts it from adding the disallowed loss to the cost of the new stock.

applied.why: Consequence for the loss is not in SOURCE; clarify the rule and route to a professional.

applied.quote: Your long-term gains fall under the 2026 0% ceiling for your filing status, so the loss cancels gains that carried no federal tax.
applied.replacement: Your 2026 taxable income, including the gain, is at or below the 0% ceiling for your filing status, so the loss cancels gain that carried no federal tax.

applied.quote: A purchase of substantially identical stock by your spouse, or by a corporation you control, after your sale also creates a wash sale.
applied.replacement: A purchase of substantially identical stock by your spouse or by a corporation you control also creates a wash sale.
applied.why: Pub. 550 and corrected F13 do not limit this to purchases after the sale.

applied.quote: If your losses exceed your gains, the [Internal Revenue Service (IRS)](https://www.irs.gov/taxtopics/tc409) lets you deduct up to $3,000 of the excess from other income each year ($1,500 if married filing separately) and carry the rest forward.
applied.replacement: If your losses exceed your gains, the [Internal Revenue Service (IRS)](https://www.irs.gov/taxtopics/tc409) lets you deduct up to $3,000 of the excess from other income each year ($1,500 if married filing separately). You carry the rest forward.
applied.why: Split the 35-word sentence; keep the first-mention link.

applied.quote: Most net capital gain is taxed at 0%, 15% or 20%, and IRS Topic 409 names higher rates for some gains: 28% for collectibles and section 1202 stock, and 25% for unrecaptured section 1250 gain.
applied.replacement: Most net capital gain is taxed at 0%, 15% or 20%. IRS Topic 409 names higher maximum rates for a few gains: 28% for collectibles and section 1202 stock, and 25% for unrecaptured section 1250 gain.
applied.why: Split the 35-word sentence and use the IRS term for maximum rates.

applied.quote: Publication 550 gives this example: you buy 100 shares of X stock for $1,000, sell them for $750 and within 30 days buy 100 shares for $800, so you cannot deduct the $250 loss and your new basis is $1,050.
applied.replacement: Publication 550 gives this example. You buy 100 shares of X stock for $1,000 and sell them for $750. Within 30 days you buy 100 shares for $800. You cannot deduct the $250 loss, and your new basis is $1,050.
applied.why: Split the 40-word sentence into readable steps.

applied.quote: The loss cancels capital gains.
applied.replacement: A capital loss on an investment cancels capital gains.

applied.quote: , using the IRS 2026 thresholds
